fields.Name: IT82 - Queue Engine Lifecycle
fields.Description: Deterministic lifecycle of the MJQueue subsystem (packages/MJQueue) against the real engine loop and the real DB substrate — no LLM calls. QU1: QueueManager.Config loads the seeded queue-type catalog plus fixture types from the live DB. QU2: the ClassFactory resolves queue-type names to the shipped drivers, including the priority-1 EntityAIActionQueue subclass. QU3: a task fed through the real AddTask/ProcessTasks/StartTask path persists Status=Completed with its Output and frees its slot. QU4: a failing ProcessTask persists Status=Failed with the JSON-serialized exception. QU5: a throwing ProcessTask cannot wedge the queue. QU6: Stop() is idempotent and a stopped queue refuses AddTask. QU7: unknown type names throw before any DB write; inactive types return undefined with zero writes. QU8: static AddTask saves its MJ: Queues row on every platform (process fields fitted to their columns) and a 'Pending' task row (fixed by the Fix_QueueTask_Status migration), and the loop completes it. QU9: with @memberjunction/work-queue-legacy-bridge imported and an Active mjqueue.<type> work-queue topic and MJQueue.LegacyQueueDriver subscription, AddTask routes the task to the durable work queue (no MJ: Queue Tasks row) and a WorkQueueHost runs it through the registered QueueBase driver, as the enqueuing user, to Completed. QU10: a routed task whose queue type has no registered driver is dead-lettered with a reason naming the missing driver.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: Queue types load from the DB, drivers resolve via the ClassFactory, the in-process loop persists task statuses (including the repaired 'Pending' insert), and legacy tasks route onto the durable work queue when their topic is activated.
